name: Soybean Crush Spread — Processing Margin & Mean Reversion
description: Tracks the soybean crush spread (gross processing margin). Formula: (ZM × 48/2000) + (ZL × 11/100) - (ZS/100), all in $/bushel. Includes seasonal analysis (average crush by calendar month) and a mean-reversion study: when March crush is >50% above the long-run March seasonal average (as in the current 84%-elevated reading), how does the spread behave into Q2? Measures forward reversion at 20d, 40d, and 63d horizons with hit rates and median drawdown.
source:
# =============================================================================
# SOYBEAN CRUSH SPREAD — PROCESSING MARGIN
# =============================================================================
# Question: How has the soybean processing margin evolved over the last 2 years?
#
# Formula (all converted to $/bushel):
#   Crush = (ZM_price × 48 lbs/2000 lbs_per_ton)
#         + (ZL_price_cents/lb × 11 lbs / 100)
#         - (ZS_price_cents/bu / 100)
#
# ZM: $/short ton  → $/bu = ZM × 48 / 2000
# ZL: cents/lb     → $/bu = ZL × 11 / 100
# ZS: cents/bu     → $/bu = ZS / 100
# =============================================================================

# --- Data: Raw futures (need continuation to get clean front-month series) ---
zs_raw = reference_futures(ticker='ZS')()
zm_raw = reference_futures(ticker='ZM')()
zl_raw = reference_futures(ticker='ZL')()

# --- Continuation: front-month continuous series (NoAdjustment preserves true price levels) ---
zs = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment
)(zs_raw.o, zs_raw.h, zs_raw.l, zs_raw.c, zs_raw.v, zs_raw.oi, zs_raw.s)

zm = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment
)(zm_raw.o, zm_raw.h, zm_raw.l, zm_raw.c, zm_raw.v, zm_raw.oi, zm_raw.s)

zl = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment
)(zl_raw.o, zl_raw.h, zl_raw.l, zl_raw.c, zl_raw.v, zl_raw.oi, zl_raw.s)

# --- Crush spread calculation (all in $/bushel) ---
# ZM is $/short ton → multiply by 48 lbs yield, divide by 2000 lbs/ton
meal_value = zm.c * 48.0 / 2000.0

# ZL is cents/lb → multiply by 11 lbs yield, divide by 100 to get dollars
oil_value = zl.c * 11.0 / 100.0

# ZS is cents/bushel → divide by 100 to get dollars
bean_cost = zs.c / 100.0

# Gross processing margin
crush = meal_value + oil_value - bean_cost

# 2-year rolling average for reference context (~504 trading days)
crush_avg = ma(period=504, type=MAType.sma)(crush)

bar_ts = index()

# --- Chart: Crush spread over time with rolling average overlay ---
xy_lines(
    title='Soybean Crush Spread — Is the Processing Margin Expanding or Compressing?',
    category='Crush Spread',
    area=True,
    y_axis_label='Crush Spread ($/bushel)',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
    y_axis_dp=2,
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='Break-Even')
    ]),
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Crush Spread', color=Color.Blue, area=True),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='2Y Average', color=Color.Orange, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, area=False)
    ]),
    order=1
)(bar_ts, crush, crush_avg)

# --- Seasonal analysis: month number for grouping ---
# datetime_extract returns 1-12; used as label for xy_bars and groupKey for summary_table RowSpec mode
month_num = datetime_extract(component=DatetimeExtractionType.month)(index())

# --- Seasonal bar chart: average crush by calendar month ---
# color_by_value not meaningful here (crush is always positive); use Blue for all bars
# Reference line at the overall long-run mean gives context for "is March high or low?"
crush_long_avg = ma(period=2520, type=MAType.sma)(crush)   # ~10Y rolling mean for reference line

xy_bars(
    title='Is March a Seasonal High or Low? — Average Crush Spread by Month',
    category='Crush Spread',
    agg=AggregationType.Mean,
    x_category_type=CategoryAxisType.Month,
    y_axis_label='Avg Crush Spread ($/bushel)',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
    y_axis_dp=2,
    data_labels=True,
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='Break-Even')
    ]),
    series=BarSeriesSchema(series=[
        BarSeriesSpec(name='Avg Crush', color=Color.Blue)
    ]),
    order=2
)(values=crush, label=month_num)

# --- Seasonal stats table: avg / high / low per month (RowSpec GROUP BY mode) ---
# 2 inputs: (values=crush, groupKey=month_num)
# Each column = one month (1-12); rows apply different aggregations
summary_table(
    category='Crush Spread',
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Seasonal Crush Spread Stats by Month ($/bushel) — All Available History',
        col_headers=['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'],
        rows=[
            RowSpec(name='Avg', agg=AggregationType.Mean, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=2),
            RowSpec(name='High', agg=AggregationType.Max, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=2),
            RowSpec(name='Low', agg=AggregationType.Min, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=2),
            RowSpec(name='Median', agg=AggregationType.Median, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=2)
        ]
    ),
    order=3
)(crush, month_num)

# --- Summary table: key levels for quick reference ---
summary_table(
    category='Crush Spread',
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Crush Spread — Key Levels ($/bushel)',
        row_size=1,
        col_size=4,
        col_headers=['Current', '2Y Average', '2Y High', '2Y Low'],
        cells=[
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Max, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=3, grid_agg=AggregationType.Min, dp=2)
        ]
    ),
    order=0
)(crush, crush, crush, crush)

# =============================================================================
# MEAN REVERSION STUDY — Elevated March Crush → Q2 Outcome
# =============================================================================
# Question: When March crush is >50% above the long-run March seasonal average
# (as in the current ~84%-elevated reading), does it mean-revert into Q2?
#
# Method:
#   1. Compute expanding historical March mean (no look-ahead bias)
#   2. Flag first bar in March where crush > 1.5× that mean
#   3. Measure forward change at +20d, +40d, +63d using lead operator (S46)
#   4. Aggregate: median reversion, hit rate (% that reverted), N events
# =============================================================================

# --- Expanding March seasonal mean (no look-ahead bias) ---
# Only accumulate March bars; ffill to carry the mean forward to all bars
is_march = month_num == 3
march_crush_only = where(is_march, crush)
march_expanding_mean = ffill(cumulative(agg=AggregationType.Mean)(march_crush_only))

# --- % deviation of current crush from long-run March seasonal mean ---
crush_vs_march_avg = (crush - march_expanding_mean) / march_expanding_mean

# --- Elevated March signal: >50% above seasonal mean, first bar of episode ---
# Using 50% threshold to capture current ~84% reading and similar historical episodes
is_elevated_march = is_valid(march_expanding_mean) and is_march and crush_vs_march_avg > 0.50

# Fire only on the FIRST bar of each elevated episode (avoid repeated signals in same month)
# is_elevated_march >> 1 = was elevated yesterday; if not, today is the first bar
is_first_elevated_bar = is_elevated_march and not (is_elevated_march >> 1)

# --- Forward crush LEVELS at 20d, 40d, 63d (lead operator — NOT forward_returns, per S46) ---
# crush << N = crush level N bars in the future
crush_20d_fwd = crush << 20
crush_40d_fwd = crush << 40
crush_63d_fwd = crush << 63

# --- Forward CHANGE in $/bushel from the elevated March reading ---
# Negative = mean reversion (crush fell); Positive = further extension
reversion_20d = crush_20d_fwd - crush
reversion_40d = crush_40d_fwd - crush
reversion_63d = crush_63d_fwd - crush

# --- Filter to elevated March event bars only (sparse — correct for xy_bars, per R12) ---
ev_rev_20d = where(is_first_elevated_bar, reversion_20d)
ev_rev_40d = where(is_first_elevated_bar, reversion_40d)
ev_rev_63d = where(is_first_elevated_bar, reversion_63d)

# --- Hit rate series: 1.0 if crush reverted (fell), 0.0 if it extended further ---
# Guard with is_valid to handle NaN at end of series (last N bars have no forward data)
hit_20d = 1.0 if (is_valid(ev_rev_20d) and ev_rev_20d < 0.0) else 0.0
hit_40d = 1.0 if (is_valid(ev_rev_40d) and ev_rev_40d < 0.0) else 0.0
hit_63d = 1.0 if (is_valid(ev_rev_63d) and ev_rev_63d < 0.0) else 0.0

# --- Event markers: one per elevated March episode ---
# Hero = crush level at signal; Subtitle = % above seasonal mean; Footer = forward outcomes
event_marker(
    schema=EventMarkerSchema(
        title='Elevated March Crush (>50% Above Seasonal Avg)',
        icon='TrendingUpIcon',
        schemas=[
            ColumnSpec(title='Crush Level ($/bu)', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot='Hero'),
            ColumnSpec(title='% Above March Avg', dp=1, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
                       card_slot='Subtitle'),
            ColumnSpec(title='+20d Change ($/bu)', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot='Details'),
            ColumnSpec(title='+63d Change ($/bu)', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot='Footer'),
            ColumnSpec(table_is_filter=True, table_visible=False)
        ]
    )
)(crush, crush_vs_march_avg, reversion_20d, reversion_63d, is_first_elevated_bar)

# --- Punchline bar chart: median forward reversion at 3 horizons ---
# Series mode (no label): each column = one horizon bar
# color_by_value=True: negative (reversion) = red, positive (extension) = green
xy_bars(
    title='Does Elevated March Crush Mean-Revert? — Avg Change at 20d / 40d / 63d',
    category='Mean Reversion',
    agg=AggregationType.Mean,
    data_labels=True,
    color_by_value=True,
    y_axis_label='Avg Forward Change in Crush ($/bushel)',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
    y_axis_dp=2,
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='No Change')
    ]),
    series=BarSeriesSchema(series=[
        BarSeriesSpec(name='+20 Trading Days', color=Color.Blue),
        BarSeriesSpec(name='+40 Trading Days', color=Color.Blue),
        BarSeriesSpec(name='+63 Trading Days (~Q2)', color=Color.Blue)
    ]),
    order=4
)(ev_rev_20d, ev_rev_40d, ev_rev_63d)

# --- Summary table: N events, median reversion, hit rate per horizon ---
# 9 inputs mapped to 3 rows (horizons) × 3 cols (Median $/bu | Hit Rate | N)
# Hit rate series (0/1) aggregated with Mean → proportion; displayed as DecimalFormat (not PercentFormat)
# because values are already 0-1 and PercentFormat would multiply by 100
summary_table(
    category='Mean Reversion',
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Mean Reversion Stats — Elevated March Crush Episodes ($/bushel change)',
        row_size=3,
        col_size=3,
        row_headers=['+20d', '+40d', '+63d (~Q2)'],
        col_headers=['Median Change ($/bu)', 'Hit Rate (reverted)', 'N Episodes'],
        cells=[
            # Row 0: +20d
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count, dp=0),
            # Row 1: +40d
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=1, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=1, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=1, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count, dp=0),
            # Row 2: +63d
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=2, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=2, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Mean, dp=2),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=2, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count, dp=0)
        ]
    ),
    order=5
)(ev_rev_20d, hit_20d, ev_rev_20d, ev_rev_40d, hit_40d, ev_rev_40d, ev_rev_63d, hit_63d, ev_rev_63d)
